profile.address: 303, North Washington Street, Bath, Morgan County, West Virginia, 25411
profile.reading:
Public records tied to this address are thin, and what is published about Morgan Wireless points to a different kind of business than the data centers, colocation suites, and enterprise server rooms that make up most of this registry. Morgan Wireless's own website describes a fixed-wireless internet service provider, not a satellite reseller, offering residential, nonprofit, and business broadband connections across the rural Eastern Panhandle of West Virginia, in and around Morgan County and Berkeley Springs (whose incorporated name is technically Bath). The company markets installation of a hardwired modem and router at the customer's premises and invites prospective subscribers to request a free site evaluation to determine whether service can reach a given location, the standard sales pattern for a wireless ISP delivering line-of-sight signal from a network of towers rather than routing data through a centralized building. The site lists a single phone number and weekday office hours but does not publish a street address for any office, tower site, or network operations center.

The coordinates recorded for this entry resolve to a location on North Washington Street in Bath, the small town more commonly known by its post office name of Berkeley Springs, the seat of Morgan County. Nothing in Morgan Wireless's own public materials confirms that this specific address houses a data center, a network operations center, or any other piece of the company's technical infrastructure - it is possible the address corresponds to a business office, a leased tower site, or simply the nearest addressable building to a wireless relay point rather than a purpose-built facility. Wireless internet providers of this size typically operate from a mix of rented rooftop and tower space spread across a service territory rather than from a single centralized data center, and Morgan Wireless's public materials give no indication that this location is an exception.

In short, this entry documents a real, operating regional internet service provider, but the public record available does not establish that the mapped address is a data center in the sense most entries in this registry describe. Readers looking for Morgan Wireless service details or coverage maps are better served by the company's own site than by treating this address as a technical facility profile.

reading.body:
This record describes a fixed wireless internet service provider, not a data center operator, and publishes no power capacity, facility specifications, or cooling infrastructure details for any physical location. Morgan Wireless's own website lists only a phone number and office hours, not a street address for Bath or any other site. The address given here comes from reverse geocoding coordinates, not from the operator's published specifications.

West Virginia has two mapped facilities in this registry and zero published megawatts across all operators. This entry cannot be ranked by capacity because no capacity is published. The state has no comparable facilities with disclosed power figures that would establish whether this location, if it were a data center, would rank among the region's infrastructure.

This record is flagged for human review to determine whether to keep, repoint, or remove it from the registry. Until the operator publishes data center specifications or a facility address on its own site, this entry does not describe a campus that matters to AI infrastructure planning.
